content: Write a regex that matches an ISO 8601 date like 2026-10-01.

Use this regex:

```
^\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])$
```

- `\d{4}` matches the four-digit year.
- `(0[1-9]|1[0-2])` matches the month, 01–12.
- `(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])` matches the day, 01–31.
- `^` and `$` anchor the match to the whole string. To find dates inside longer text, replace them with `\b`.

It checks the format and the ranges, but it doesn't check the calendar. For example, it accepts `2026-02-31`. To reject that, parse the match with a date library.

If you also want to accept the basic format (`20261001`), the extended-only version above won't match it. Say so and I'll add it.
